item.base_system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy buttons prepared by vacuum arc melting
item.intervention: Gravity casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP)
item.processing: Vacuum arc melting, gravity casting into bars, HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile tests, compression tests, creep tests at 982 °C under 200 MPa and 120 MPa
item.structure_change: Single-phase BCC before HIP; after HIP, a secondary HCP phase (ZrHf-rich) appeared, evenly dispersed in the matrix
item.property_change: Hardness increased from 323.5 ± 6.5 HV to 437.2 ± 11.6 HV; materials found to be highly brittle under tension with elongation below machine detection limit
item.attributed_mechanism: The HIP process is responsible for the appearance of the HCP phase, likely due to slow cooling allowing eutectoid reaction or precipitation of HCP component from the BCC phase
quotes: The HIP process is responsible for the appearance of a Hexagonal Close Packed (HCP) phase that is dispersed differently in these two castings.
The elongation to fracture under tension was below the machine's detection limit and therefore could not be measured.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy buttons prepared by vacuum arc melting. Intervention: Gravity casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP). Processing: Vacuum arc melting, gravity casting into bars, HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile tests, compression tests, creep tests at 982 °C under 200 MPa and 120 MPa. Structure change: Single-phase BCC before HIP; after HIP, a secondary HCP phase (ZrHf-rich) appeared, evenly dispersed in the matrix. Property change: Hardness increased from 323.5 ± 6.5 HV to 437.2 ± 11.6 HV; materials found to be highly brittle under tension with elongation below machine detection limit. Mechanism: The HIP process is responsible for the appearance of the HCP phase, likely due to slow cooling allowing eutectoid reaction or precipitation of HCP component from the BCC phase. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The HIP process is responsible for the appearance of a Hexagonal Close Packed (HCP) phase that is dispersed differently in these two castings."

item.base_system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy buttons prepared by vacuum arc melting
item.intervention: Suction-assisted casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP)
item.processing: Vacuum arc melting, suction-assisted casting using a vacuum pump, HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile tests, compression tests, creep tests at 982 °C under 200 MPa and 120 MPa
item.structure_change: Single-phase BCC before HIP; after HIP, a secondary HCP phase (ZrHf-rich) appeared, concentrated mostly at the grain boundaries
item.property_change: Hardness increased from 330.2 ± 9.8 HV to 509.1 ± 13.5 HV; materials found to be highly brittle under tension with elongation below machine detection limit
item.attributed_mechanism: The difference in hardness and microstructure may be related to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase, which is concentrated mainly at the grain boundaries in the suction-assisted casting
quotes: Contrary to the compression properties, both materials were found to be highly brittle under tension, either during room temperature tension tests or creep tests conducted at 282 °C.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy buttons prepared by vacuum arc melting. Intervention: Suction-assisted casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP). Processing: Vacuum arc melting, suction-assisted casting using a vacuum pump, HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h. item.base_system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy in gravity-cast condition (before HIP)
item.processing: HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h
item.test_conditions: Microhardness testing, XRD analysis, SEM imaging
item.structure_change: Transition from single-phase BCC to a two-phase microstructure containing BCC and HCP phases
item.property_change: Hardness increased from 323.5 ± 6.5 HV to 437.2 ± 11.6 HV
item.attributed_mechanism: The hardness increase after HIP can be related to the appearance of the secondary HCP phase and its influence on dislocation mobility, similarly to precipitation hardening
quotes: Note that both materials were single phased before undergoing HIP, while a darker phase is discernible inside the bright matrix after HIP.
The hardness increase after HIP can be related to the appearance of the secondary HCP phase and its influence on dislocation mobility, similarly to precipitation hardening.
The HIP process also led to a considerable increase in the mechanical properties of both materials under compression

item.processing: HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h

item.processing: Machining of dog-bone specimens, manual polishing
item.structure_change: Fracture is inter-crystalline accompanied by intergranular cracking, most intensive at the center of the specimen
item.property_change: Elongation to fracture below machine detection limit; uniform grain size observed on fracture surface compared to gravity cast
item.attributed_mechanism: The lack of any evidence of plastic deformation in both gravity and suction-assisted casting is in line with the non-detectable elongations to fracture
quotes: The fracture of the suction-assisted casting is accompanied by intergranular cracking, which is most intensive at the center of the specimen.
The grain size of the gravity casting varies significantly between the different regions of the fracture surface, while in the case of the suction-assisted casting the grain size is quite uniform.
The lack of any evidence of plastic deformation in both gravity and suction-assisted casting is in line with the non-detectable elongations to fracture.

item.test_conditions: Creep at 982 °C under 200 MPa and 120 MPa
item.structure_change: Brittle fracture with porous grains and brittle cracked grains; surface contaminated with oxidation products
item.property_change: Failed after short periods of time of 15 min (200 MPa) and 90 min (120 MPa)
item.attributed_mechanism: The high concentration of oxides beneath the surface detected in the broken creep specimens may be due to preexisting surface cracks through which the oxidation process occurred
quotes: Two creep tests at 982 °C were conducted on gravity-cast specimens, the first under a load of 200 MPa and the second under 120 MPa. Both failed after short periods of time of 15 and 90 min, respectively.
Figure 5 and Figure 6 show that the fracture is brittle. As revealed by EDS analysis, the surface is contaminated with oxidation products, mainly at the near-surface regions of the sample.
High concentration of oxides observed beneath the surface of the broken creep specimens may point to preexisting surface cracks through which the oxidation process occurred.

item.processing: Stationary Rigaku Smart Lab diffractometer with Cu tube (λ Kα = 1.5406 Å)
item.structure_change: Identification of two phases: NbTaTi-based BCC and ZrHf-based HCP
item.attributed_mechanism: The ZrHf solid solution phase is comprised of HCP elements (at room temperature), it has an HCP structure and thus exhibits the characteristic X-ray diffraction pattern of other HCP phases
quotes: Based on the above described SEM study, which indicates the presence of two major phases in the case of the HfNbTaTiZr alloy that has undergone HIP, each peak was associated with one of these two phases: a roughly equimolar solid solution of ZrHf and a solid solution of NbTaTi
As ZrHf solid solution phase is comprised of HCP elements (at room temperature), it has an HCP structure and thus exhibits the characteristic X-ray diffraction pattern of other HCP phases.
The current study offers clear evidence of the existence of both a BCC and an HCP phase.

item.intervention: Comparison of gravity-cast vs. suction-assisted cast microstructures
item.processing: SEM and EDS analysis of HIP'ed specimens
item.structure_change: HCP phase evenly dispersed in gravity cast; HCP phase concentrated at grain boundaries in suction-assisted cast
item.property_change: Hardness of suction-assisted cast (509.1 HV) greater than gravity cast (437.2 HV) after HIP
item.attributed_mechanism: The difference between the suction-assisted cast and the gravity cast may be related to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase
quotes: It should be noted that the dark phase is evenly dispersed in the matrix of the gravity-assisted casting, while in the case of the suction-assisted casting it is concentrated mostly at the grain boundaries.

As for the materials that underwent HIP, it is clear that the HIP process increased the hardness of both castings. Nevertheless, in the case of the materials that underwent HIP, the hardness of the suction-assisted casting was found to be greater than that of the gravity cast.

The difference between the suction-assisted cast and the gravity cast may be related to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase, which is evenly dispersed in the case of the gravity casting while concentrated mainly at the grain boundaries in the case of the suction-assisted casting.

Property change: Hardness of suction-assisted cast (509.1 HV) greater than gravity cast (437.2 HV) after HIP. Mechanism: The difference between the suction-assisted cast and the gravity cast may be related to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase. Evidence: measured. item.structure_change: Brittle cracked grains and porous grains observed; surface contamination with oxidation products
item.property_change: Premature failure (90 min) compared to aerospace requirements (>50 h for MAR-M-247)
item.attributed_mechanism: The high concentration of oxides beneath the surface detected in the broken creep specimens may be due to preexisting surface cracks through which the oxidation process occurred
quotes: Figure 5 depicts a SEM micrograph showing a general view of the fracture surface of a specimen that crept at 982 °C under 120 MPa.
Two main types of broken grains can be seen at the fracture surface: brittle cracked grains and porous grains.
For the sake of comparison, according to MAR-M-247 material specifications for the aerospace industry [ [10] , [11] ], the time to rupture of the material should exceed 50 h under 200 MPa at 982 °C.
